- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (sentiment > 0.6) — reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to sentiment strength.
- Underestimate prices after sharp spikes (sentiment drops below 0.3) — adjust downward by 3–8% to avoid overcorrection.
- Lagged forecasts tend to overreact to recent sentiment — apply a 1–3 day smoothing filter to reduce momentum bias.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast exceeds 3σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 10–15% to align with historical volatility.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment > 0.7 and forecast > 10% above prior 5-day high, cap forecast at 10% below prior peak.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate mid-term volatility — reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
